item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: 'Crazy': Moderates fear Dem leadership promised far-left reparations and ICE demands in turn of votes
item.description: House Democrats are split as progressives push to abolish ICE and reparations for descendants of slavery, while moderates warn it may hurt affordability.
item.content:encoded:
Progressive House Democrats believe party leaders could use their newly won majority to back their far-left agenda on such matters as reparations and abolishing ICE, despite pushback from moderates concerned about the party's direction.

Newly elected Democratic Caucus Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., and progressive lawmakers told Fox News Digital that proposals to ICE, expand deportation protections and pursue slavery reparations will be part of the party's legislative discussions under Speaker nominee Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., despite concerns from moderates that the agenda could distract from affordability.

‘SQUAD’ MEMBER ANNOUNCES ‘MAJORITY PRIORITIES’ INCLUDING REPARATIONS, ABOLISHING ICE AFTER BLUE WAVE

"Jeffries has been very clear, he wants to make sure everyone in the caucus is well represented," Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, told Fox News Digital.

Lieu told Fox News Digital that he is "excited" to have "discussions on everything" with members of the caucus, including proposals involving reparations and abolishing ICE.

The California Democrat said he would also be willing to consider other priorities of Rep. Ayanna Presley, D-Mass., including "Medicare for All," "abortion justice" and extending Temporary Protected Status for Third World migrants.

'SQUAD' MEMBER URGES DEMS TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF MIDTERM SWEEP BY PASSING FAR-LEFT POLICIES

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., a prominent supporter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), told Fox News Digital that progressives and House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries have found common ground on several priorities outlined in Pressley's agenda, including expanding healthcare access and public housing.

"Of course, there are going to be areas where leader Jeffries and DSA are going to be in strong opposition, but there are also areas like expanding Medicaid, public housing, and housing issues in general, where there are shared values that unite everybody," Ocasio-Cortez, a potential 2028 presidential contender, told Fox News Digital.

Ocasio-Cortez has also begun working with Democratic leadership on the House Energy and Commerce Committee to advance her healthcare priorities, a senior congressional democratic staffer told Fox News Digital.

However, moderate Democrats were skeptical that party leadership would embrace the progressive agenda, with some questioning whether Jeffries and other leaders had promised to consider those demands in exchange for support during the leadership elections.

"Our agenda is to focus on costs," Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., told Fox News Digital. "What's clear is we had an overwhelming majority. I think some of my colleagues seem to be unhappy with winning in a place we've never won before."

Gottheimer accused progressive colleagues of wanting to "squawk and complain and make their demands" rather than focus on the issues that helped Democrats win the midterm elections.

The New Jersey Democrat also rejected proposals to "defund police, have open borders, or get rid of the United States Senate," arguing that neither he nor Democratic leadership would support such policies.

HAKEEM JEFFRIES REJECTS MEDICARE FOR ALL, DSA AGENDA AS RO KHANNA CALLS HEALTH PLAN 'MOST IMPORTANT PRIORITY'

Gottheimer, an outspoken critic of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), suggested that Pressley's priorities more closely resemble the organization's platform than the broader Democratic Party's agenda.

"The DSA, they have their own agenda," Gottheimer said.

RADICAL SOCIALIST WING'S HUGE NIGHT REVEALS ASCENDING CLOUT WITHIN DEMOCRATIC PARTY

Another Democratic lawmaker, who requested anonymity, told Fox News Digital that they and a longtime colleague viewed the prospect of leadership adopting the progressive agenda as "crazy."

The lawmaker also speculated that Lieu and Jeffries were expressing openness to progressive proposals to avoid opposition during Wednesday's leadership elections.

Jeffries and Pressley did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Colts turned down Daniel Jones trade offer considered not good, then cut the QB and got nothing in return
item.description: Daniel Jones was blindsided by his Indianapolis Colts release after the team rejected a Baltimore Ravens trade offer just two weeks earlier, a source said.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts walked away from starting quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday to the surprise of some, including Jones himself, because only two weeks earlier the club spurned a trade offer by the Baltimore Ravens and promised Jones he would remain their quarterback.

Those new details from one of the more curious personnel juggling episodes by an NFL team recently is evidence the Colts do not have their act fully together.

Jones was expecting to remain with the Colts for the remainder of the regular season and was surprised that would no longer be the case when he was told of his release on Friday, a source told OutKick.

DANIEL JONES, JONATHAN TAYLOR REACT TO COLTS FIRE SALE AS THEY REMAIN PUT: 'YOU'RE NOT HAPPY TO SEE IT'

But the quarterback was indeed released and now must wait until Monday to see if he is claimed, which will decide a new team for him, or clears waivers which will allow him to make a decision on what team he joins and when.

If Jones clears waivers, a source said he and his representatives will study the landscape to see if a team that is in the playoff hunt or likely headed to the playoffs needs him as either a backup or a replacement for an injured starter.

Jones and his reps didn't think it would come to this.

Before the trade deadline on Nov. 10, the Colts told Jones he was staying with the team because he was not being traded. That didn't mean there wasn't interest.

MORE PROOF THAT ANY TEAM TRADING FOR DANIEL JONES AT THE NFL TRADE DEADLINE IS CHASING FOOL'S GOLD

As OutKick reported in the lead-up to the trade deadline, Jones was the subject of trade talks. And over the weekend it was confirmed that the Ravens not only showed interest in Jones but made an offer for him.

The offer: A 2027 fourth-round pick for Jones and a 2027 fifth-round pick, as first reported by ESPN.

COLTS HAD JONATHAN TAYLOR AND GROVER STEWART TRADE OFFERS BUT DIDN'T COMPLETE DEALS THAT EVENTUALLY GOT PULLED

The Colts, however, turned down the offer.

This was the same Colts that when all was done after the trade deadline, had traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson, and receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. So, the Colts kept their quarterback while choosing to strip away talent around him.

The Colts privately said just after the deadline the issue with not trading Jones then was they weren't being offered good value in return.

This, of course, seems a ridiculous stance now.

Firstly, the offer by the Ravens was not necessarily a final offer, according to a league source. There were days remaining before the trade deadline, including a weekend of games, before those two teams ended their talks about Jones.

And, indeed, the Ravens made a trade for Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett as a fallback to getting Jones. The deal they made with the Cardinals was better than the one they offered the Colts because the Cardinals continued to negotiate with Baltimore about a deal.

The Ravens eventually gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick for Brissett and a 2028 seventh-rounder in return.

But the greater point is the Colts, 10 days after the trade deadline, after telling Jones he was staying, and declining an offer to trade him because it was deemed not good enough, then cut Jones.

For nothing.

Zero.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

It is in fact worse than zero because a trade would have sent Jones and his current year base salary obligations to the Ravens. Waiving him leaves Indianapolis paying his remaining base salary if he goes unclaimed, as expected.

And, of course, if the Colts thought getting a fourth-rounder for Jones was unacceptable 10 days ago, now they are without Jones and don't get that fourth-rounder in return in next April's draft.

The Colts have been the subject of talk among NFL executives for a couple of weeks. And, as it was prior to the trade deadline, that discussion is not flattering.

item.title: Remembering Fiona: Timeline of how the hippo beat the odds, became a star and inspired millions
item.description: From a 29-pound preemie to a global star that inspired millions around the world, the Cincinnati Nile hippo Fiona boosted zoo attendance before her sudden death. Here's a timeline of her life.
item.content:encoded:
Millions of Americans are mourning the loss of Fiona.

The 9-year-old Nile hippo who captured the hearts of people all over the country after surviving an early birth in January 2017 and becoming the world's first premature hippo to be raised by humans died at the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden on Thursday, Nov. 19, after ingesting a visitor's knitted hat that was accidentally deflected into her enclosure.

Born six weeks early at just 29 pounds, Fiona rapidly drew enthusiastic online followers. She also helped push annual attendance at the zoo as fans traveled from far and wide to catch a glimpse of the spunky creature. 

Her death occurred roughly a decade after another high-profile demise at the same zoo, when Harambe, a 17-year-old western lowland gorilla, was fatally shot by zoo staff in May 2016 after a young boy climbed into his enclosure.

BELOVED HIPPO FIONA DIES AT CINCINNATI ZOO AFTER SWALLOWING VISITOR'S HAT

The Cincinnati Zoo on Friday released new autopsy findings after Fiona's death.

A postmortem examination determined that a foreign object, confirmed to be a hat that zoo officials said accidentally wound up in her enclosure, was lodged deep inside the hippo's massive digestive tract, according to the zoo's director of animal health, Dr. Mike Wenninger.

The hat was lodged halfway through her small intestine, roughly 25 feet past her stomach and still 50 feet from exiting her body.

Zoo visitors, local and federal leaders, and fans all around the world are still trying to absorb news of the animal's passing.

"I was really mad," a young woman in downtown Cincinnati told Fox News Digital on Friday. "I know it was a fluke accident … but it just seemed like it could have been prevented in some way. And she was just so iconic. This is just devastating to the community."

The woman added, "I was really upset. I went home from work after that."

Fiona has had books written about her, murals painted of her and even clothing with cute depictions of her created in her honor. The city of Cincinnati has considered her its unofficial mascot. 

Fiona came into the world on Jan. 24, 2017, under extraordinary circumstances.

The hippo was born six weeks before she was due. She "was too small to stand and nurse from her mom, Bibi," according to the Cincinnati Zoo.

She weighed a mere 29 pounds at birth — 25 pounds lighter than the lowest recorded birth weight for Nile hippos, according to the zoo.

"The zoo's care team had to step in and figure out how to feed her, what to feed her, how to keep her warm, and how to manage critical care 24/7 while juggling other daily responsibilities," the zoo's website states.

"It took a village, but #TeamFiona did it!"

Fiona's father, Henry, was 35 years old when she was born (he died in Oct. 2017). Bibi was 17. Fiona was the first Nile hippo to be born at the Cincinnati Zoo in over 50 years.

Fiona experienced a big year of growth in 2018.

LOCH NESS MONSTER SIGHTINGS JUMP IN 2026 AS SCIENTIST DRILLS INTO LEGENDARY MYSTERY

By her first birthday, Jan. 24, 2018, she tipped the scales at 650 pounds.

She also attracted a lot of attention during this period.

"By sharing her ups and downs with the world (every day for almost two years), she became a beloved symbol of hope and a source of inspiration for millions of people," the zoo's website states.

By her third birthday in Jan. 2019, she weighed half a ton — with zoo officials describing her as a "thousand-pound toddler."

Fiona's half-brother, Fritz, was born to Bibi on Aug. 3, 2022, fathered by a male named Tucker.

BABY ELEPHANT MAKES HISTORIC ARRIVAL AT SMITHSONIAN'S NATIONAL ZOO AS FIRST BIRTH IN NEARLY 25 YEARS

The zoo documented when Fiona and baby Fritz first met three weeks later.

"Five-year-old Fiona was curious but took her cues from her mom, Bibi, and backed off when Fritz got almost close enough for a nose boop," the zoo said.

"This first intro went very well. Bibi was appropriately protective of Fritz but was not aggressive toward Fiona," the Cincinnati Zoo's animal care director, Christina Gorsuch, said at the time. 

"The exposure was brief but a great first step."

At the beginning of 2025, Fiona celebrated her eighth birthday.

Speaking to Fox News Digital, a Cincinnati man said on Friday, "She wasn’t supposed to be here to begin with. The fact that she overcame so much … it was always inspiring. And to see her with her family, you know, mom, dad, half-brother — it was always nice to see."

Reflecting on the hippo's early life, Cincinnati Zoo marketing manager Amy LaBarbara said that she was an instant social media hit.

"We shared updates on Fiona on social media every day during the first year of her life, and people couldn’t get enough," LaBarbara said at the time. 

"We even tried to stop at one point but got so much pushback that we kept up with the daily posts."

LaBarbara said that "posts about Fiona and her little brother Fritz consistently [got] millions of views and likes from a global audience."

On Thursday, Nov. 19, Cincinnati Zoo officials announced that Fiona had died after a visitor's hat was tossed in the air and a ceiling fan deflected it over the hippo enclosure's viewing glass.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"The vet staff tried everything they could to help her after she ingested a hat that ended up in her habitat by accident last week," the statement read. 

"Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome," officials added.

The zoo said Fiona's team "performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover."

Second lady Usha Vance, a mother of four, paid a heartbreaking tribute to Fiona after the hippo died.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Vance shared a touching family photo of one of her children visiting Fiona as she mourned the death of the world-famous hippo.

"We are so sad," she wrote in part on Instagram. 

Fiona would have been 10 years old in Jan. 2027.

"In those 10 years, she inspired millions with her story of survival and did so much to raise awareness and caring for her species," the zoo said. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"She was truly treasured."

Zoo officials have asked the public to "keep the people who worked with Fiona and tried to save her in your thoughts and prayers."

"They loved her and did their best to save her," the statement added. 

"They are also, understandably, asking for space at this time."

Gorsuch, the director of animal care, said Fritz and the zoo's other hippos, Bibi and Tucker, have been eating and behaving normally since Fiona's death. 

The area around the Hippo Cove was to be closed throughout the weekend. The animal care team were "shaken and trying to navigate this loss," the zoo said. 

"We come here every Saturday morning," a dad in Cincinnati told Fox News Digital on Friday about the zoo. "We grew up with Fiona. Our two kids — we have a membership here. And [Fiona] was always a staple of why we came over."

Melissa Rudy, Louis Casiano and Bonny Chu, all of Fox News Digital, contributed reporting.

item.title: Penn State finds new low as Rutgers' last-gasp touchdown ends 38-year drought against Nittany Lions
item.description: Rutgers football stunned the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium as A.J. Surace's last-second drive ended a 38-year losing streak in the series.
item.content:encoded:
The Penn State Nittany Lions were playing for a berth in the College Football Playoff national championship in January 2025 and were on the brink of beating the Notre Dame Fighting Irish to get that spot.

Fast forward nearly two years later, the team may have suffered one of its worst losses.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penn State was hoping to defend Happy Valley against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights – a team they had beaten every time they had played since 1988. Rutgers had not had much success since moving to the Big Ten Conference but showed signs of life in Greg Schiano’s second stint at head coach. While the 2026 season had gone awry, Rutgers could hang its hat on Saturday’s result.

The Scarlet Knights pulled off an epic comeback to stun the Nittany Lions, 25-24.

It started with an Antwan Raymond 13-yard touchdown run to cut the deficit to 24-17 with 10:19 left in the game. Rutgers forced Penn State to punt the ball back to them with 1:37 remaining in the game. Scarlet Knights quarterback A.J. Surace led the team on an 11-play, 67-yard drive to score a touchdown with no time remaining on the clock.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The play itself was almost as unbelievable as writing "Rutgers beat Penn State."

Surace tossed the ball to Raymond, who was met by a swarm of blue jerseys. Raymond made a heads-up play to pitch the ball to Ben Black III, who scored the touchdown. It brought Rutgers to within one point of the lead.

Schiano determined in that moment there was nothing to lose by going for the win. Surace threw a pass to DK Gilley, who found the end zone and gave Rutgers the absolutely stunning victory.

The 38-year streak is over. You have to give Schiano a ton of credit for laying it all out there and having confidence in the offense to try to gut out the victory in regulation instead of trying to spend any more time in Beaver Stadium than was absolutely necessary.

The 2026 season is absolutely one to forget for Rutgers. But the Scarlet Knights will always have Nov. 21, in which they topped Penn State on the road.

item.title: What really happens when you need help restoring your identity
item.description: Identity theft restoration involves credit freezes, fraud alerts and disputing fraudulent records. Here's how the recovery process works, step by step.
item.content:encoded:
Identity theft restoration takes more than one phone call. It often means securing accounts, documenting fraudulent activity and working with several companies to correct inaccurate records.

The term "identity restoration" can sound complicated until you suddenly need it. Maybe someone opened a credit card in your name, took over your bank account or used your personal information to get medical care. Now you're dealing with unfamiliar charges, paperwork and companies that all seem to have different requirements.

Fortunately, knowing what happens during recovery can make the process easier to manage. Here's how identity restoration typically works, what you may need to do yourself and where professional help can make a difference.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT

Identity restoration usually starts with understanding the problem. A specialist may ask when you first noticed suspicious activity, which accounts someone accessed and whether you lost money or personal information. These details help identify the type of identity theft involved. Someone opening a credit card in your name requires a different response than a criminal taking over your phone number or using your medical information. A restoration specialist can help you separate confirmed fraud from suspicious activity that still needs investigation. As a result, you can focus on the companies and accounts that need attention first.

Before tackling paperwork, focus on preventing additional damage. Depending on what happened, you may need to contact your bank, lock a credit card, change passwords or secure your mobile phone account. If someone accessed your email, make securing that account an early priority. Criminals can use compromised email accounts to reset passwords and gain access to other services. You may also want to place a fraud alert or freeze your credit.

Neither option fixes fraud that has already occurred. However, both can help reduce the risk of additional new-account fraud.

One of the most frustrating parts of identity theft recovery is having to explain the same problem repeatedly. A case file helps you keep track of important information and avoid starting over with every phone call. Include dates of suspicious activity, copies of statements, confirmation numbers, correspondence and the names of representatives you've contacted. Also, record what each company promised to do and when you should expect a response. This becomes especially helpful when several organizations are involved. For example, your bank might close an account while a fraudulent balance still appears on your credit report. Having documentation gives you a clear record of the steps you've already completed. Keep those records somewhere secure. Additionally, avoid sending sensitive documents through unverified email addresses or links.

Depending on the type of fraud, identity restoration may involve banks, creditors, credit bureaus, mobile carriers, medical providers or government agencies. Each organization follows its own procedures. A bank may ask you to complete a fraud affidavit, while a credit bureau may request an identity theft report before blocking fraudulent information. A restoration specialist can explain those requirements and help you navigate the process. In some situations, the specialist may also coordinate communications or work with institutions on your behalf. However, you may still need to verify your identity, provide documents or authorize certain actions. Restoration assistance helps you work through the process, but the affected institutions remain responsible for reviewing claims and correcting their records.

Once you secure your accounts and identify the affected organizations, the next step involves correcting the damage. If someone opened a fraudulent credit account, you may need to dispute the information with the creditor and the credit bureaus. The Federal Trade Commission recommends reporting identity theft through IdentityTheft.gov, where you can create an FTC Identity Theft Report and receive a personalized recovery plan. An FTC Identity Theft Report can also help you exercise important rights, including requesting that credit bureaus block information resulting from identity theft. Medical identity theft may require contacting healthcare providers and insurers to correct inaccurate records. Meanwhile, tax identity theft generally involves working directly with the IRS. Keep copies of every document you submit. Whenever possible, request written confirmation after an organization resolves an issue.

Identity theft recovery rarely happens all at once. Your bank might reverse a fraudulent transaction before a credit bureau finishes investigating a related account. Similarly, a phone carrier may restore your number, but you may still need to strengthen account security to prevent another takeover. That's why follow-ups are so important. Set reminders for promised responses and continue checking your statements, accounts and credit reports after the initial incident. You can review your credit reports for free each week at AnnualCreditReport.com. Even after you resolve a case, additional suspicious activity can surface if criminals continue trying to use your stolen information.

WAS YOUR IDENTITY STOLEN? WHAT TO DO IN THE FIRST 24 HOURS

Not every identity theft case follows the same path. The type of fraud determines which organizations need to get involved and what steps you should take. For example, new-account fraud often involves creditors and credit bureaus. An existing bank-account takeover requires immediate attention from the financial institution, while medical identity theft may involve correcting treatment and billing records. Tax or government benefits fraud can require separate reporting procedures. And if a scammer convinced you to authorize a payment, your options may differ from those available for unauthorized account transactions. That's why identifying the problem early is important. A credit freeze may help protect against new credit accounts, but it cannot correct a medical record or recover money sent to a scammer.

Identity theft recovery can feel slow, especially when you're waiting for several companies to respond. However, you can track progress by focusing on specific actions rather than expecting everything to happen immediately. Have you secured the compromised account? Did you report the fraudulent charge? Has the credit bureau acknowledged your dispute? Each completed step helps move the case forward. If a company misses a deadline or provides conflicting information, your case file will help you explain the situation without starting the conversation from scratch.

Before speaking with a restoration specialist or fraud department, gather any suspicious statements, letters, alerts or emails connected to the incident. The company may also ask you to provide identification, an FTC Identity Theft Report or written authorization allowing someone to assist with your case. Always verify that you're communicating with the legitimate organization before sharing sensitive information. Also, ask why a document is necessary and how the company plans to handle it. Ultimately, you should understand what information you're providing and what actions someone may take on your behalf.

If you've experienced identity theft, handling multiple disputes and follow-up calls yourself can become overwhelming. That's where an identity protection service may help. Some services provide access to identity restoration specialists who can guide you through the recovery process. Depending on the provider and your plan, specialists may help organize documentation, explain next steps and assist with communications involving affected institutions.

Identity protection services may also monitor certain personal information, credit reports and financial accounts. Alerts can help you discover suspicious activity before it leads to additional problems. However, identity monitoring cannot detect every form of fraud, and restoration assistance cannot guarantee that every dispute will end in your favor. The benefit comes from having experienced support when you're trying to work through a complicated situation.

Beyond restoration assistance, some identity protection services offer tools that help you identify suspicious activity, reduce the exposure of personal information and respond when something looks wrong. Features vary by provider and plan, so it's worth checking what's included before signing up.

Some services offer tools that help you identify merchants and websites that may have your payment card information on file. Reviewing these connections can help you decide where to remove stored payment details, especially if you no longer use certain accounts. However, these tools cannot automatically confirm whether someone has stolen your card information.

Certain identity protection services can monitor eligible financial accounts and flag transactions that appear unusual or potentially fraudulent. These might include unfamiliar purchases or unexpected charges. An alert gives you an opportunity to review the transaction and contact your financial institution if necessary. Keep in mind that these services may not detect every suspicious transaction.

Some identity protection services include tools that search covered data broker websites for your personal information and submit removal requests on your behalf. Reducing publicly available information may help limit your exposure to identity theft and scams. However, no removal service can erase your information from every website or guarantee that it will never reappear.

Some providers offer access to support specialists or online tools that can help you evaluate suspicious messages, websites and financial activity. Depending on the service, you may receive guidance on reporting scams, securing accounts and taking steps to recover from identity theft.

Certain plans may also include reimbursement benefits for eligible losses or expenses, subject to coverage limits and exclusions. However, these services cannot guarantee that you'll recover money you sent to a scammer. Always review the terms before relying on a particular benefit.

See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com

When someone steals your identity, discovering the fraud is often only the beginning. The real work comes afterward, when you're trying to secure accounts, correct records and get answers from companies handling different parts of the problem. I've always believed that knowing what to do next can make a stressful situation much easier to handle. Start by protecting the accounts you still control, document everything and use the free recovery tools available through the FTC. If you want additional help, an identity protection service with restoration specialists may help you navigate the recovery process and stay organized. No service can promise an instant fix, but having experienced support can make a difference when you're dealing with identity theft.

item.title: Shane Beamer shares bizarre explanation as to why LaNorris Sellers didn't walk for South Carolina senior night
item.description: Shane Beamer kept LaNorris Sellers out of senior night, then admitted he didn't know how the South Carolina quarterback was listed on the roster.
item.content:encoded:
South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers is listed as a senior on the team's official roster and is set to graduate in December. Those are facts one would assume that Shane Beamer would be aware of, but that doesn't appear to be the case for the Gamecocks' head coach.

"I made that decision. Seniors walk, he's not a senior" Beamer explained. "Now he’s graduating, but he’s not a senior, so we talked about it and if I’m the bad guy, I’m the bad guy. But there’s a lot of guys that have been here since 2023 that aren’t technically seniors, so that’s on me, sorry."

Beamer doubled down with his claim that Sellers isn't technically a senior, before then admitting that he didn't actually know how the quaterback was listed on the roster.

"If you look at our roster, I think they’re listed as a senior, are they not?" Beamer asked the room. "I think LaNorris is listed as a redshirt junior? How is he listed? I don’t even know. To be fair to Beamer, understanding college eligibility and what year certain players are has never been more complicated. On the flip side of that, if Sellers, who we can assume is well aware of his classification status, voiced that he wanted to walk alongside his fellow seniors and had that proposition shut down by Beamer because he wasn't 'technically' a senior in his mind, then it's an even worse look on the head coach.

Sellers is widely regarded as a first-round prospect heading into the 2027 NFL Draft; he'll get over the fact that he wasn't recognized as a senior. The entire situation is also a rather perfect microcosm of Sellers' time playing in Columbia under Beamer's up-and-down tenure.

item.title: Mississippi mother, caregiver face charges after refusing to give cancer treatment to toddler
item.description: Destiny Schliefert faces felony murder charges after police say she refused cancer treatment for her 3-year-old son, who weighed 24 pounds when he died.
item.content:encoded:
A Mississippi mother is facing multiple felony murder charges after she refused to give her 3-year-old son his cancer treatment, authorities say.

The mother, Destiny Schliefert, reported the death of her son to police on July 31, saying the boy had stopped breathing. He weighed just 24 pounds by the time of his death, police said.

The boy had been diagnosed with cancer at Children’s Mercy Hospital in Kansas City in March 2024. Schliefert told police that the boy's health began to rapidly decline in May, with him losing the ability to eat and walk.

STARVING TODDLER ATE DIAPERS AND DRYWALL BEFORE DYING IN FILTHY ROOM WHILE PARENTS LIVED CLEAN, POLICE SAY

Police say she claimed he had stopped eating because he'd been impacted by his grandfather's death in 2025.

She did not pursue any treatment for the boy's cancer after his diagnosis in 2024.

SOUTH CAROLINA MOM COULDN'T REMEMBER LAST TIME SHE FED 2 DAUGHTERS BEFORE THEY WERE FOUND DEAD: AFFIDAVITS

A doctor told investigators that the boy, who has not been identified, likely would have lived if he had received treatment. Schliefert herself admitted that medical care "probably" would have helped him.

She told police that she and another caregiver, Debbie Potter, drove the boy to the hospital in early July but didn't bring him in, fearing they would be reported for poorly caring for the boy, according to Ozark First.

PARENTS OF 7-YEAR-OLD WHO DIED WEIGHING 255 POUNDS CHARGED WITH MURDER IN SUSPECTED NEGLECT CASE

Phone records indicate that Schliefert searched "fastest way to get a toddler to gain weight fast" on July 2, just weeks before the boy died.

Schliefert faces charges of second-degree murder, second-degree felony murder and child abuse or neglect resulting in death.

Schliefert also has two additional children, ages 7 and 15. She faces additional child endangerment charges in connection to their care.

item.title: Robert Pattinson becomes seventh actor to play James Bond in franchise's 60-year history
item.description: Robert Pattinson becomes the seventh James Bond, joining a legacy from Sean Connery's 1962 "Dr. No" to Daniel Craig's 2021 "No Time to Die."
item.content:encoded:
Robert Pattinson officially stepped into cinema’s most famous tuxedo as the seventh actor to play James Bond, joining a group of Hollywood legends who defined 007 for generations.

The casting marks the latest chapter in a more than 60-year cinema legacy that began with Sean Connery in 1962 and most recently saw Daniel Craig retire the tuxedo in 2021's "No Time to Die."

Before Pattinson takes his first sip of a shaken martini, we are looking back at every actor who previously held the iconic license to kill — from the modern-day action stars to the original 1960s trailblazers.

ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND

Daniel Craig took over as James Bond in "Casino Royale" in 2006, delivering one of the franchise's most dramatic reinventions. The English actor's casting initially sparked debate among the spy's fans, but his intense physical performance and emotionally layered portrayal helped establish a new direction for the iconic spy.

Craig starred in five Bond films: "Casino Royale," "Quantum of Solace," "Skyfall," "Spectre" and "No Time to Die." His version of Bond was more vulnerable and psychologically complex, with an interconnected storyline exploring the character's relationships, personal losses and loyalty to MI6.

Craig concluded his 15-year run with "No Time to Die," marking one of the most consequential endings in the franchise's history.

Pierce Brosnan became James Bond in 1995 with the release of "GoldenEye." The Irish actor helped introduce the legendary spy to a new generation of moviegoers.

Along with "GoldenEye," Brosnan starred in "Tomorrow Never Dies," "The World Is Not Enough" and "Die Another Day." Following his departure from the franchise, Brosnan continued his Hollywood career with projects including "Mamma Mia!," "The Ghost Writer" and "Black Adam."

The year 1987 brought yet another James Bond, played by Timothy Dalton. The Welsh actor brought a darker and more serious tone to the franchise. Dalton developed his acting career through theater, television and film before becoming 007.

Dalton appeared in two Bond films, "The Living Daylights," and "Licence to Kill." His portrayal moved away from the humor associated with Roger Moore and focused more heavily on espionage, revenge and realistic action.

Roger Moore took over the role in 1973 with the premiere of "Live and Let Die." The British actor brought a lighter, more humorous approach to the spy, differing from Connery's original tougher interpretation.

Moore portrayed Bond in seven films, more than any other actor in the franchise. In addition to "Live and Let Die," he starred in "The Man with the Golden Gun," "The Spy Who Loved Me," "Moonraker," "For Your Eyes Only" and "Octopussy."

His final appearance as Bond came with "A View to a Kill" in 1985.

George Lazenby took over the role of James Bond after Sean Connery left the franchise. The Australian actor appeared in "On Her Majesty's Secret Service." At 29 when the film premiered, he became the youngest actor to portray Bond in the official film franchise.

Lazenby's portrayal of Bond focused more on his romantic side, particularly through Bond's relationship with Tracy di Vicenzo.

Although the film received mixed reviews upon release, it has since developed a strong following among Bond fans. Lazenby chose not to return for another installment, making him the only actor to portray Bond in just one official film.

Sean Connery became the first official James Bond when he starred in "Dr. No" in 1962. The Scottish actor helped turn Ian Fleming's fictional British spy into Hollywood's most recognizable action star.

Connery starred in six official Bond films, including "From Russia with Love," "Goldfinger," "Thunderball," "You Only Live Twice" and "Diamonds Are Forever." He also appeared in the unofficial Bond film, "Never Say Never Again."

item.title: Kirk Cousins and the Vikings aim to upset the 8-1 49ers in NFL Mexico City Game
item.description: Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings meet Brock Purdy's 49ers on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City, with Purdy an MVP candidate this season.
item.content:encoded:
We have a bit of a double dip here for "Sunday Night Football." We also have the two teams playing in the NFL Mexico City Game.

It is hard to even keep track of where the games are played any longer because every week there is some sort of different location. In any case, that’s what we have tonight as the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers.

The Vikings are one of the best teams in football, and I have to say I was dead wrong about how Kirk Cousins would perform for them. Cousins, in his return to the Vikings, completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns last week. He did give up one interception, but the offense was actually moving the ball, and Justin Jefferson was involved in the offense as they scored 30 points and beat the Packers. That’s improvement no matter how you look at it.

This win over the Packers came after back-to-back losses to the Lions and the Bills. In those games, they only allowed a total of 42 points combined, but they scored just 21. Something had to be done, and this defense is definitely Super Bowl quality.

Perhaps they can ride that, and the new arm under center all the way. I do still have a hard time believing that Cousins is the answer, but he has a better cushion with this defense than he has ever had before.

KIRK COUSINS AND THE MINNESOTA VIKINGS ARE REUNITED AND IT FEELS SO GOOD AFTER WIN OVER GREEN BAY PACKERS

The 49ers are arguably the best team in football, and we could be seeing an NFC Championship preview with these two on the field. The 49ers are 8-1, with their lone loss coming on a somewhat predictable trip to Atlanta a few weeks ago.

The team was kind of due for a loss, and it happened. In the past two weeks, they’ve been able to dominate the Raiders and the Cowboys. Dallas put up plenty of points against the 49ers, but they couldn’t stop San Francisco in any way, shape, or form.

Brock Purdy has looked like an MVP candidate this season. He has thrown for 2,369 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. They added Keenan Allen at the deadline to help shore up their receiving issues. However, I’m not sure it even matters.

As long as Christian McCaffrey stays healthy, that is the only guy who really matters on their offense. He does a bit of everything as evidenced by the 223 total yards and three touchdowns he had last week against Dallas. Oddly enough, it was the first time all season that he eclipsed 100 yards either receiving or rushing this year.

I do wonder if the advantage of this game goes to the 49ers or Cousins for them having played each other on November 8th. Cousins was with an entirely different offense, so he gets to see the same defense as before. San Francisco has already seen how Cousins plays this season, but he does have different weapons.

Either way, I think this is not going to be the shootout we’ve seen. I think this will be more of a defensive battle, which is what the Vikings want. Give me the under in this one.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jared Goff power Lions offense into Week 11 game against Buccaneers
item.description: The 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 2-0 in the division and hope Bucky Irving's running game can steal it despite Baker Mayfield's struggles this season.
item.content:encoded:
Week 11 of the NFL season brings us that much closer to the playoffs. Looking at the standings, there are still a lot of things to be decided. Sure, we can make an assumption about certain teams making or missing the postseason. I’m looking forward to seeing where this season ends up.

The Tampa Buccaneers are hopeful they can stumble their way into the postseason, and the Detroit Lions are playing in the best division of football.

The Buccaneers are 3-6 for the season with some very frustrating losses this year. Baker Mayfield looked great the past few years but has been a disaster this season. In fairness to him, part of the issue is that he has been injured. However, there are also some games where he just doesn’t look like himself. I suppose we can blame not having Mike Evans any longer, but that should only be to a certain extent. Emeka Egbuka doesn’t look as impressive as he did in his first season. Bucky Irving has looked phenomenal, though.

If the Buccaneers can keep riding the running game to wins, they might have a solid chance of stealing this division. Coming into this week, the Panthers are leading the division with four victories. That puts Tampa, with three wins, in second place. They are also the only team in the division with a positive point differential. To their credit, they are also 2-0 in their division.

I wouldn’t say their schedule has been overly difficult, so we will see where things end up, but there is still a good chance for them to find their way into the postseason, even if they lose today.

PANTHERS WR TETAIROA MCMILLAN IS SICK OF NFL MEDIA 'DISRESPECTING' THE NFC SOUTH OVER LOSING RECORDS

The Lions are almost comical with what happens to their team sometimes. Last week, their best defender, Aidan Hutchinson, sacked Drake Maye and then hurt himself celebrating the sack. That gives them nine defensive players on their depth chart who are now on the injured list or out for the game. This was already a thin defense that didn’t have a ton of room for error. It is now in an even worse spot.

The Lions are one of the worst teams against the pass, but have been good against the run.

The offense has been fantastic once again. Jared Goff is up to 2,437 passing yards, 18 touchdowns, and four interceptions for the season. Jahmyr Gibbs has established himself as one of the best weapons in football with 1,000 rushing yards on almost 200 carries and 11 rushing touchdowns.

Amon-Ra St. Brown has caught seven touchdowns with 755 receiving yards. That trio is among the best in football and can make any defense struggle. Tampa has one of the better passing defenses in the game, and is very strong against the run. So it could be a bit of a struggle for Detroit.

LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY

We’ve seen Detroit be capable of winning low-scoring games – they did it over the Vikings recently. However, that’s really not the way they prefer to win. They want a shootout. I just don’t see them running up and down the field over the Buccaneers.

Tampa could keep this close, but ultimately, I think the Lions are the right side. Give me Detroit -6.5.
